Tūī, Prosthemadera novaeseelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A blackbird-sized honeyeater that looks black at a distance but shines blue, green and bronze in good light. Two curled white tufts hang at the throat, with a lacy collar of fine white feathers on the neck.

In this photo: Two white throat tufts (poi), iridescent blue-green and bronze sheen, slender curved bill.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A blackbird-sized honeyeater that looks black at a distance but shines blue, green and bronze in good light. Two curled white tufts hang at the throat, with a lacy collar of fine white feathers on the neck.

media.alt: A glossy dark bird with white throat tufts sits upright on a flower stalk, head raised and bill open, against green bush
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tui_(Prosthemadera_novaeseelandiae)_Tiritiri_Matangi.jpg

items.context:
Korimako (bellbird), Anthornis melanura, is found only in New Zealand. A slim, olive-green honeyeater with a short curved bill, a slightly forked tail and red eyes. It has no white tufts or wing bars.

In this photo: Olive-green body, purple gloss on head, dark wing and tail, slightly curved black bill, red eye.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A slim, olive-green honeyeater with a short curved bill, a slightly forked tail and red eyes. It has no white tufts or wing bars.

media.alt: An olive-green songbird with a darker purple-glossed head and black wing tips perches on a thin twig
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:New_Zealand_bellbird_(Anthornis_melanura)_male_Tiritiri_Matangi.jpg

items.context:
Hihi (stitchbird), Notiomystis cincta, is found only in New Zealand. A small, fast-moving honeyeater that often cocks its tail like a wren, with a bold white wing bar and a thin, down-curved bill.

In this photo: Velvet-black head with white ear tufts, yellow shoulder band, white wing bar, thin dark bill.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small, fast-moving honeyeater that often cocks its tail like a wren, with a bold white wing bar and a thin, down-curved bill.

media.alt: A small black-headed bird with a white ear tuft and a bright yellow band across the shoulder perches on a twig
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Male_hihi_perched_on_a_twig,_raising_its_white_ear_tufts.jpg

items.context:
Kererū (New Zealand pigeon), Hemiphaga novaeseelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A very large pigeon with iridescent green, bronze and purple upperparts sharply cut off from a clean white breast, and a red bill, eyes and feet.

In this photo: Large size, sharp border between green-bronze neck and white breast, red bill and feet.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A very large pigeon with iridescent green, bronze and purple upperparts sharply cut off from a clean white breast, and a red bill, eyes and feet.

media.alt: A large plump bird with a white breast and a shining green head faces the camera from a branch
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:New_Zealand_pigeon_(Hemiphaga_novaeseelandiae)_Waitakere.jpg

items.context:
Pīwakawaka (New Zealand fantail), Rhipidura fuliginosa, is found only in New Zealand. A small, restless bird that constantly fans its long tail. The common pied form has a grey head, white eyebrows, black and white bands on the throat and a cinnamon belly; the rare black form is almost all sooty black.

In this photo: Fanned tail with white edges, white eyebrow, buff-orange belly, small size.

Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand (CC0).

practices.explanation: A small, restless bird that constantly fans its long tail. The common pied form has a grey head, white eyebrows, black and white bands on the throat and a cinnamon belly; the rare black form is almost all sooty black.

media.alt: A small grey-brown bird with a white eyebrow holds its long tail spread like a fan above a log
media.credit: Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand, CC0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_New_Zealand_fantail_(Rhipidura_fuliginosa)_(26323434203).jpg

items.context:
Riroriro (grey warbler), Gerygone igata, is found only in New Zealand. A tiny, slim bird, olive-grey above and pale grey to off-white below, with a bright red eye and a fine black bill. The darker tail has white tips that show as a band in flight, and it often hovers at the edge of foliage.

In this photo: Very small; plain grey-brown upperparts, pale grey face and breast, bright red eye.

Photo: Rosa Stewart (CC0).

practices.explanation: A tiny, slim bird, olive-grey above and pale grey to off-white below, with a bright red eye and a fine black bill. The darker tail has white tips that show as a band in flight, and it often hovers at the edge of foliage.

media.alt: A tiny grey bird with pale grey underparts and a red eye perches on a twig
media.credit: Photo: Rosa Stewart, CC0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A_Grey_Warbler_near_the_waters_of_the_Mawaihakona_Stream.jpg

items.context:
Tauhou (silvereye), Zosterops lateralis, is native, having reached New Zealand on its own. A small olive-green songbird with an obvious ring of white feathers around the eye, a grey back and pinkish-buff flanks.

In this photo: Ring of white feathers around the eye, olive-green head and wings, grey back, pinkish-buff flanks.

Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small olive-green songbird with an obvious ring of white feathers around the eye, a grey back and pinkish-buff flanks.

media.alt: A small olive-green bird with a white ring around its eye and buff flanks perches on a bare branch
media.credit: Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_silvereye_or_wax-eye_(Zosterops_lateralis)_(51626662516).jpg

items.context:
Miromiro (tomtit), Petroica macrocephala, is found only in New Zealand. A small, big-headed forest bird with short legs and a white wing bar that often perches on low branches. Males show a small white spot above the bill.

In this photo: Black head, back and throat, white spot above the bill, white wing bar, yellow-orange breast (South Island male).

Photo: Colin Meurk (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A small, big-headed forest bird with short legs and a white wing bar that often perches on low branches. Males show a small white spot above the bill.

media.alt: A small black-and-white bird with a big head and a yellow breast perches on a lichen-covered branch
media.credit: Photo: Colin Meurk, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Petroica_macrocephala_macrocephala_55598510.jpg

items.context:
Toutouwai (North Island robin), Petroica longipes, is found only in New Zealand. A dark grey, upright, long-legged songbird with a pale patch on the lower breast and belly, often feeding on the ground and approaching people closely.

In this photo: Upright stance, long thin legs, dark grey plumage with pale cream lower breast patch.

Photo: Tony Wills (CC BY 2.5).

practices.explanation: A dark grey, upright, long-legged songbird with a pale patch on the lower breast and belly, often feeding on the ground and approaching people closely.

media.alt: A dark grey songbird with long legs and a pale lower breast stands on a branch
media.credit: Photo: Tony Wills, CC BY 2.5, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NZ_North_Island_Robin-2.jpg

items.context:
Tītitipounamu (rifleman), Acanthisitta chloris, is found only in New Zealand. New Zealand's smallest bird: almost tailless, with a fine, slightly upturned bill and a pale eyebrow. It creeps up trunks and flicks its wings constantly.

In this photo: Tiny, near-tailless; plain bright green back and head, white eyebrow, thin upturned bill.

Photo: amamo (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: New Zealand's smallest bird: almost tailless, with a fine, slightly upturned bill and a pale eyebrow. It creeps up trunks and flicks its wings constantly.

media.alt: A tiny bright yellow-green bird with almost no tail and a white eyebrow perches on a twig
media.credit: Photo: amamo, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/329952750

items.context:
Pōpokotea (whitehead), Mohoua albicilla, is found only in New Zealand. A small, compact North Island songbird with a white head and underparts, brown-grey back, wings and tail, and a short dark bill. It usually travels in noisy flocks.

In this photo: White head and underparts contrasting with light brown wings and back, short pale bill, dark eye.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A small, compact North Island songbird with a white head and underparts, brown-grey back, wings and tail, and a short dark bill. It usually travels in noisy flocks.

media.alt: A small sparrow-sized bird with a white head and breast and a brown back perches among broad leaves
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Whitehead_(Mohoua_albicilla)_Tiritiri_Matangi.jpg

items.context:
Mohua (yellowhead), Mohoua ochrocephala, is found only in New Zealand. A small South Island forest songbird with a bright canary-yellow head and breast, brown back, wings and tail, and a black bill and legs.

In this photo: Bright yellow head and breast, olive-brown wings and back, short black bill.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small South Island forest songbird with a bright canary-yellow head and breast, brown back, wings and tail, and a black bill and legs.

media.alt: A small bird with a bright canary-yellow head and breast perches on a broken branch tip
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mohua_perched_on_a_tree_branch_(Ulva_Island).jpg

items.context:
Kōkako, Callaeas wilsoni, is found only in New Zealand. A large blue-grey songbird with a black face mask and small, bright blue wattles hanging from the base of the bill. It has long legs and a long tail and bounds through branches more than it flies.

In this photo: Blue-grey plumage, black mask around the eye and bill base, bright blue wattles, long legs and tail.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A large blue-grey songbird with a black face mask and small, bright blue wattles hanging from the base of the bill. It has long legs and a long tail and bounds through branches more than it flies.

media.alt: A slate-grey bird with a black face mask and a blue wattle below the bill perches side-on on a branch
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kokako_perched_on_a_branch_1.jpg

items.context:
Tīeke (saddleback), Philesturnus rufusater (North Island) and Philesturnus carunculatus (South Island), is found only in New Zealand. A glossy black songbird with a chestnut 'saddle' across the back and rump and fleshy orange-red wattles at the corners of the bill. North Island birds have a thin pale yellow line along the front edge of the saddle.

In this photo: Black plumage, chestnut saddle and rump, red-orange fleshy wattles at the gape, strong pointed bill.

Photo: Judi Lapsley Miller (CC BY 4.0).

practices.explanation: A glossy black songbird with a chestnut 'saddle' across the back and rump and fleshy orange-red wattles at the corners of the bill. North Island birds have a thin pale yellow line along the front edge of the saddle.

media.alt: A glossy black bird with a chestnut saddle across its back and red wattles at the bill perches on a branch
media.credit: Photo: Judi Lapsley Miller, CC BY 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:20180625_Zealandia_074_DxO.jpg

items.context:
Ruru (morepork), Ninox novaeseelandiae, is native to New Zealand. A small, dark-brown owl with large yellow eyes set in a darker face, a white-spotted back and a streaky brown and cream breast.

In this photo: Small owl, dark brown plumage with buff spots and streaks, big yellow eyes in a darker facial mask.

Photo: JJ Harrison (CC BY-SA 3.0).

practices.explanation: A small, dark-brown owl with large yellow eyes set in a darker face, a white-spotted back and a streaky brown and cream breast.

media.alt: A small brown bird with large forward-facing yellow eyes and a spotted breast perches on a branch at night
media.credit: Photo: JJ Harrison, CC BY-SA 3.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Morepork_0A2A7676.jpg

items.context:
Kākā, Nestor meridionalis, is found only in New Zealand. A large olive-brown forest parrot with a grey-white crown, a heavy grey bill, crimson belly and under-tail, and red-orange under the wings.

In this photo: Big parrot, scalloped olive-brown plumage, crimson-red belly and underwing, grey crown, heavy grey bill.

Photo: Nil NZ (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large olive-brown forest parrot with a grey-white crown, a heavy grey bill, crimson belly and under-tail, and red-orange under the wings.

media.alt: A large olive-brown bird with a hooked grey bill and crimson under its body feeds on palm seed stalks
media.credit: Photo: Nil NZ, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:K%C4%81k%C4%81_in_Nikau_palm_02.jpg

items.context:
Kea, Nestor notabilis, is found only in New Zealand. A large olive-green mountain parrot with scalloped feathers, a long narrow grey-black upper bill and scarlet-orange under the wings.

In this photo: Olive-green scalloped plumage, long narrow upper bill, dark cere and eye-ring (adult).

Photo: Michal Klajban (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large olive-green mountain parrot with scalloped feathers, a long narrow grey-black upper bill and scarlet-orange under the wings.

media.alt: A large olive-green bird with a long hooked bill stands on a rock in the mountains
media.credit: Photo: Michal Klajban, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kea_by_Mueller_Hut,_Aoraki_-_Mount_Cook_National_Park,_New_Zealand_22.jpg

items.context:
Kākāpō, Strigops habroptilus, is found only in New Zealand. A very large, flightless, night-active parrot with moss-green plumage mottled with yellow and black, and a pale, owl-like whiskered face.

In this photo: Very large and stocky, moss-green plumage finely barred black and yellow, owl-like facial disc, pale bill.

Photo: Laura Molles (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A very large, flightless, night-active parrot with moss-green plumage mottled with yellow and black, and a pale, owl-like whiskered face.

media.alt: A large, plump moss-green bird with a pale whiskered face and hooked bill climbs a branch at night
media.credit: Photo: Laura Molles, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/943764

items.context:
Kākāriki (red-crowned parakeet), Cyanoramphus novaezelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A bright emerald-green, long-tailed parakeet with a crimson forehead and crown, a crimson stripe through the eye, a red patch on each side of the rump and blue on the wing edge.

In this photo: Bright green body, crimson crown and stripe through the eye, violet-blue flight feathers, long tail.

Photo: Judi Lapsley Miller (CC BY 4.0).

practices.explanation: A bright emerald-green, long-tailed parakeet with a crimson forehead and crown, a crimson stripe through the eye, a red patch on each side of the rump and blue on the wing edge.

media.alt: A bright green long-tailed bird with a crimson forehead and blue wing edge perches on a thin branch
media.credit: Photo: Judi Lapsley Miller, CC BY 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Red-crowned_parakeet_-_K%C4%81k%C4%81riki_-_at_Zealandia_EcoSanctuary.jpg

items.context:
Pīpīwharauroa (shining cuckoo), Chrysococcyx lucidus, is native to New Zealand. A sparrow-sized cuckoo with shining metallic green upperparts and white underparts crossed by dark green-bronze bars. No other New Zealand bird is iridescent green like this.

In this photo: Iridescent bronze-green upperparts, white face and underparts barred with dark green-brown bands.

Photo: Caiden (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A sparrow-sized cuckoo with shining metallic green upperparts and white underparts crossed by dark green-bronze bars. No other New Zealand bird is iridescent green like this.

media.alt: A small bird with a metallic green back and white underparts with bold dark bars perches on a twig
media.credit: Photo: Caiden, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/247059436

items.context:
Koekoeā (long-tailed cuckoo), Urodynamis taitensis, is found only in New Zealand. A large, hawk-like cuckoo with a very long barred tail, brown upperparts barred and spotted rufous, and pale underparts heavily streaked dark brown.

In this photo: Tail nearly as long as the body and barred rufous, white underparts with heavy dark streaks, hawk-like shape.

Photo: Ben Weatherley (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large, hawk-like cuckoo with a very long barred tail, brown upperparts barred and spotted rufous, and pale underparts heavily streaked dark brown.

media.alt: A brown bird with a very long barred tail and heavily streaked underparts clings to a tree in beech forest
media.credit: Photo: Ben Weatherley, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/36149765

items.context:
Kārearea (New Zealand falcon), Falco novaeseelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A compact, fast falcon with long pointed wings, a long tail, a dark eye and a dark moustache stripe below it. It is dark brown above with a streaked cream breast and rufous thighs.

In this photo: Yellow eye-ring, cere and feet; dark slate-brown back, streaked cream breast, rufous thighs.

Photo: Tony Wills (CC BY-SA 3.0).

practices.explanation: A compact, fast falcon with long pointed wings, a long tail, a dark eye and a dark moustache stripe below it. It is dark brown above with a streaked cream breast and rufous thighs.

media.alt: A dark brown bird of prey with rufous thighs and a streaked breast perches on a branch, looking sideways
media.credit: Photo: Tony Wills, CC BY-SA 3.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NZ_Falcon_-_Karearea_01.JPG

items.context:
Kāhu (swamp harrier), Circus approximans, is native to New Zealand. A large, long-legged hawk that glides low with wings raised in a shallow V and often perches on roadside posts or feeds on roadkill. It shows a pale rump in flight.

In this photo: Pale buff underparts with dark streaks, pale face and nape, yellow eye (adult), long yellow legs.

Photo: iancoull (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large, long-legged hawk that glides low with wings raised in a shallow V and often perches on roadside posts or feeds on roadkill. It shows a pale rump in flight.

media.alt: A large pale-brown hawk with a streaky buff breast and yellow eyes stands at the edge of a road
media.credit: Photo: iancoull, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/357067434

items.context:
Kiwi, the five species of the genus Apteryx, are found only in New Zealand. A round, flightless, wingless-looking bird with shaggy, hair-like brown feathers streaked darker, a very long pale bill with nostrils at the tip, and short sturdy legs. Mostly active at night.

In this photo: Hair-like streaky brown plumage, no visible wings or tail, very long slender bill with nostrils at the tip, stout legs.

Photo: Caiden (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A round, flightless, wingless-looking bird with shaggy, hair-like brown feathers streaked darker, a very long pale bill with nostrils at the tip, and short sturdy legs. Mostly active at night.

media.alt: A round, shaggy dark-brown bird with no visible wings probes the leaf litter at night with a long thin bill
media.credit: Photo: Caiden, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/296716229

items.context:
Weka, Gallirallus australis, is found only in New Zealand. A hen-sized, flightless brown rail with black streaks, a strong pointed bill, sturdy legs and red eyes. It is bold and curious around people.

In this photo: Hen-sized flightless rail, mottled brown plumage streaked black, strong reddish-brown bill, red-brown eye.

Photo: JJ Harrison (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A hen-sized, flightless brown rail with black streaks, a strong pointed bill, sturdy legs and red eyes. It is bold and curious around people.

media.alt: A chicken-sized brown bird with a stout pinkish bill walks across a mossy rock
media.credit: Photo: JJ Harrison, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:0A2A9595_Weka.jpg

items.context:
Takahē, Porphyrio hochstetteri, is found only in New Zealand. A huge, plump, flightless rail with deep blue head and breast, olive-green back and wings, a massive red bill and forehead shield, and thick red legs.

In this photo: Very stout body, deep blue head and breast, olive-green back, huge red bill and frontal shield, thick red legs.

Photo: JJ Harrison (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A huge, plump, flightless rail with deep blue head and breast, olive-green back and wings, a massive red bill and forehead shield, and thick red legs.

media.alt: A large, plump blue and olive-green bird with a massive red bill and red legs walks across grass
media.credit: Photo: JJ Harrison, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:South_Island_Takah%C4%93_0A2A9204.jpg

items.context:
Pūkeko, Porphyrio melanotus, is native to New Zealand. A tall, long-legged swamp hen with a deep violet-blue head and breast, black back, red bill and forehead shield, and a white under-tail that it flicks as it walks.

In this photo: Deep violet-blue head and breast, black back, red bill and frontal shield, long orange legs, white under the tail.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A tall, long-legged swamp hen with a deep violet-blue head and breast, black back, red bill and forehead shield, and a white under-tail that it flicks as it walks.

media.alt: A long-legged purple-blue and black bird with a red bill and red forehead shield walks on grass
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Australasian_swamphen_(Porphyrio_melanotus)_Tiritiri_Matangi.jpg

items.context:
Whio (blue duck), Hymenolaimus malacorhynchos, is found only in New Zealand. A slate blue-grey duck of fast mountain rivers, with chestnut spots on the breast, yellow eyes and a pale grey-pink bill with a soft black flap at the tip.

In this photo: Blue-grey plumage, chestnut flecks on breast, pale pinkish-white bill with black flaps at the tip, yellow eye.

Photo: Sebastian Doak (CC BY 4.0).

practices.explanation: A slate blue-grey duck of fast mountain rivers, with chestnut spots on the breast, yellow eyes and a pale grey-pink bill with a soft black flap at the tip.

media.alt: A slate-grey duck with a pale pinkish-white bill stands in a fast-flowing stream
media.credit: Photo: Sebastian Doak, CC BY 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hymenolaimus_malacorhynchos_276148332.jpg

items.context:
Pūtangitangi (paradise shelduck), Tadorna variegata, is found only in New Zealand. A large, goose-like duck of paddocks and lakes with a large white patch on the upper wing and a chestnut under-tail. Pairs are often seen together, and the two sexes look very different.

In this photo: All-dark head with green gloss, dark finely barred body, white wing patch and chestnut undertail.

Photo: Michal Klajban (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large, goose-like duck of paddocks and lakes with a large white patch on the upper wing and a chestnut under-tail. Pairs are often seen together, and the two sexes look very different.

media.alt: A large dark duck with a glossy black-green head and white and chestnut wing patches stands at the water's edge
media.credit: Photo: Michal Klajban, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Paradise_shelduck_(male),_Lake_Victoria,_Christchurch_06.jpg

items.context:
Pāpango (New Zealand scaup), Aythya novaeseelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A small, dark, round diving duck that floats like a cork and dives often, with a blue-grey bill.

In this photo: Glossy black-purple head and back, bright yellow eye, blue-grey bill with black tip, compact diving-duck shape.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small, dark, round diving duck that floats like a cork and dives often, with a blue-grey bill.

media.alt: A small glossy black diving duck with a bright yellow eye and blue-grey bill swims on calm water
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:New_Zealand_Scaup_(male),_swimming_in_calm_water.jpg

items.context:
Pāteke (brown teal), Anas chlorotis, is found only in New Zealand. A small, dark-brown dabbling duck with an obvious white ring around the eye and a green patch on the wing.

In this photo: Small dark-brown dabbling duck, distinct white eye-ring, green speculum on wing.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A small, dark-brown dabbling duck with an obvious white ring around the eye and a green patch on the wing.

media.alt: A small brown duck with a white ring around its eye swims on a brown pond
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Brown_teal_(Anas_chlorotis)_Tiritiri_Matangi.jpg

items.context:
Kōtuku (white heron), Ardea alba modesta, is native to New Zealand. A tall, pure-white heron with a very long, kinked neck, long dark legs and a long yellow bill (dark when breeding). The gape line runs back past the eye.

In this photo: Large all-white heron, long dagger-like yellow bill, very long kinked neck, long black legs.

Photo: William Harland (CC BY 4.0).

practices.explanation: A tall, pure-white heron with a very long, kinked neck, long dark legs and a long yellow bill (dark when breeding). The gape line runs back past the eye.

media.alt: A tall pure-white wading bird with a long yellow bill and very long neck lands on a rock beside blue water
media.credit: Photo: William Harland, CC BY 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/274495522

items.context:
Matuku moana (white-faced heron), Egretta novaehollandiae, is native, having reached New Zealand on its own. A slim, medium-sized blue-grey heron with a white face and throat, a dark dagger bill and yellow legs. Very common in paddocks, estuaries and ponds.

In this photo: Blue-grey body, white face and throat, long yellow legs, slim dark bill, wispy back plumes.

Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A slim, medium-sized blue-grey heron with a white face and throat, a dark dagger bill and yellow legs. Very common in paddocks, estuaries and ponds.

media.alt: A slender blue-grey wading bird with a white face and yellow legs walks through shallow water
media.credit: Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_white-faced_heron_(Egretta_novaehollandiae)_(52507412140).jpg

items.context:
Kōtuku ngutupapa (royal spoonbill), Platalea regia, is native, having reached New Zealand on its own. A large white wading bird with a long, flat black bill that widens into a spoon at the tip, black facial skin and black legs. It sweeps its bill from side to side when feeding.

In this photo: White plumage, long black flat bill widening to a spoon at the tip, black legs, nuchal plumes.

Photo: Ben Ackerley (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large white wading bird with a long, flat black bill that widens into a spoon at the tip, black facial skin and black legs. It sweeps its bill from side to side when feeding.

Poaka (pied stilt), Himantopus himantopus leucocephalus, is native to New Zealand. A slim black-and-white wader on extremely long pink legs, with a needle-thin black bill and black on the back of the neck.

In this photo: Very long bright pink legs, needle-thin black bill, white head and underparts, black back and wings, black hind-neck collar.

Photo: Rick Barricklow (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A slim black-and-white wader on extremely long pink legs, with a needle-thin black bill and black on the back of the neck.

media.alt: A black-and-white wader on extremely long pink legs walks through shallow water
media.credit: Photo: Rick Barricklow, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/193011428

items.context:
Kōtare (sacred kingfisher), Todiramphus sanctus vagans, is native to New Zealand. A stocky, big-headed bird with a large black bill, turquoise-green back, buff to cream underparts, a white collar and a broad black stripe through the eye. Often perches hunched on wires or posts over water or open ground.

In this photo: Green-blue back and wings, white collar, buff-cream underparts, black eye stripe, broad black bill.

Photo: Ben Ackerley (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A stocky, big-headed bird with a large black bill, turquoise-green back, buff to cream underparts, a white collar and a broad black stripe through the eye. Often perches hunched on wires or posts over water or open ground.

media.alt: A stocky bird with a turquoise-green back, buff underparts and a long black bill holds a crab on a rock
media.credit: Photo: Ben Ackerley, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/171692404

items.context:
Tōrea pango (variable oystercatcher), Haematopus unicolor, is found only in New Zealand. A large, heavy shorebird with a long bright orange bill, red eye with an orange eye-ring and stout coral-pink legs. Upperparts are black; underparts range from all black through smudgy to white.

In this photo: Entirely black plumage, long straight bright orange bill, red eye with orange eye-ring, stout coral-pink legs.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large, heavy shorebird with a long bright orange bill, red eye with an orange eye-ring and stout coral-pink legs. Upperparts are black; underparts range from all black through smudgy to white.

media.alt: An all-black shorebird with a long bright orange bill and pink legs stands on a shingle beach
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Variable_oystercatcher_(Haematopus_unicolor)_Tiritiri_Matangi.jpg

items.context:
Tūturiwhatu (New Zealand dotterel), Anarhynchus obscurus (Charadrius obscurus on NZ Birds Online), is found only in New Zealand. A large, heavy-billed plover of sandy beaches, grey-brown above, with underparts that turn rich rusty orange in the breeding season and are pale outside it.

In this photo: Large plover, rich orange-rust underparts (breeding), grey-brown back, heavy black bill, pale eyebrow.

Photo: Amaya M. (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large, heavy-billed plover of sandy beaches, grey-brown above, with underparts that turn rich rusty orange in the breeding season and are pale outside it.

media.alt: A plump plover with grey-brown back and a rusty-orange breast stands on a beach
media.credit: Photo: Amaya M., CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/130032729

items.context:
Pohowera (banded dotterel), Anarhynchus bicinctus (Charadrius bicinctus on NZ Birds Online), is found only in New Zealand. A small, compact plover, plain brown above and white below. In breeding plumage it has a narrow dark neck band above a broad chestnut breast band.

In this photo: Crisp black upper band and broad chestnut lower band, black line through the eye and above white forehead.

Photo: Samuel Amaris (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A small, compact plover, plain brown above and white below. In breeding plumage it has a narrow dark neck band above a broad chestnut breast band.

media.alt: A small plover with a narrow black neck band above a broad chestnut breast band stands on sand
media.credit: Photo: Samuel Amaris, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/240509177

items.context:
Tarāpunga (red-billed gull), Chroicocephalus novaehollandiae scopulinus, is native to New Zealand. A small white gull with a pale grey back, white-spotted black wing tips, a white eye and bright red bill, eyelids and legs.

In this photo: Small gull, bright red bill, legs and eye-ring, pale grey back, black wing tips with white spots.

Photo: Michal Klajban (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A small white gull with a pale grey back, white-spotted black wing tips, a white eye and bright red bill, eyelids and legs.

media.alt: A small pale-grey and white seabird with a bright red bill and red legs stands on a rail
media.credit: Photo: Michal Klajban, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Red-billed_gull,_New_Brighton,_New_Zealand.jpg

items.context:
Karoro (southern black-backed gull), Larus dominicanus, is native to New Zealand. A big gull with a black back and upper wings, white head and underparts, a heavy yellow bill with a red spot near the tip and pale greenish legs.

In this photo: Large gull, black back and upperwings, white head and body, heavy yellow bill with red spot, greenish-yellow legs.

Photo: Tony Wills (CC BY 2.5).

practices.explanation: A big gull with a black back and upper wings, white head and underparts, a heavy yellow bill with a red spot near the tip and pale greenish legs.

media.alt: A large white seabird with a jet-black back and wings and a heavy yellow bill stands on a ledge by the water
media.credit: Photo: Tony Wills, CC BY 2.5, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Black_backed_gull_02.jpg

items.context:
Tākapu (Australasian gannet), Morus serrator, is native to New Zealand. A large white seabird with a buff-yellow head, long pointed wings with black trailing edges, and a pale blue-grey dagger bill outlined in black. It plunge-dives for fish and nests in dense colonies.

In this photo: White plumage, golden-yellow head, long pale blue-grey bill outlined in black, blue eye-ring.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A large white seabird with a buff-yellow head, long pointed wings with black trailing edges, and a pale blue-grey dagger bill outlined in black. It plunge-dives for fish and nests in dense colonies.

media.alt: Two white seabirds with golden-buff heads and pale dagger bills touch bills at a colony
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Close-up_of_gannet_pair_in_colony.jpg

items.context:
Hoiho (yellow-eyed penguin), Megadyptes antipodes, is found only in New Zealand. A tall penguin with yellow eyes and a pale yellow band running from the eyes around the back of the head, a slate-blue back, white front and a reddish bill.

In this photo: Pale yellow band from the eye around the back of the head, yellow eye, slate-grey back, white front, pink feet.

Photo: Christian Mehlführer, User:Chmehl (CC BY 2.5).

practices.explanation: A tall penguin with yellow eyes and a pale yellow band running from the eyes around the back of the head, a slate-blue back, white front and a reddish bill.

media.alt: A tall flightless seabird with a pale yellow band around its head and a white front stands on a rocky shore
media.credit: Photo: Christian Mehlführer, User:Chmehl, CC BY 2.5, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Yellow-eyed_Penguin_MC.jpg

items.context:
Kororā (little penguin), Eudyptula minor, is native to New Zealand. The smallest penguin: slate-blue to indigo above and white below, with no head markings and a dark hooked bill.

In this photo: Very small penguin, blue-grey upperparts, white underparts, no head markings, dark bill.

Photo: William Harland (CC BY 4.0).

practices.explanation: The smallest penguin: slate-blue to indigo above and white below, with no head markings and a dark hooked bill.

media.alt: A very small flightless seabird with slate-blue upperparts and a white front stands among rocks
media.credit: Photo: William Harland, CC BY 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/177780340

items.context:
Kawaupaka (little shag), Microcarbo melanoleucos, is native to New Zealand. A small shag with a short, stubby yellow bill and a long tail. Plumage varies: most are black with white cheeks and throat, some are fully white below (pied), and a few are smudgy in between.

In this photo: Small shag, short stubby yellow bill, white cheeks and throat, black body, long tail, small forehead crest.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small shag with a short, stubby yellow bill and a long tail. Plumage varies: most are black with white cheeks and throat, some are fully white below (pied), and a few are smudgy in between.

media.alt: A small black cormorant with a white throat, a short yellow bill and a small crest stands on a rock by the sea
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Little_Shag_standing_on_a_rock.jpg

items.context:
Toroa (northern royal albatross), Diomedea sanfordi, is found only in New Zealand. A huge albatross with a white body, head and back, entirely black upper wings and a massive pale pink bill with a black cutting edge.

In this photo: Very large albatross, white body and head, all-black upperwing, massive pale pinkish bill with dark cutting edge.

Photo: Sandy Thomas (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A huge albatross with a white body, head and back, entirely black upper wings and a massive pale pink bill with a black cutting edge.

media.credit: Photo: Sandy Thomas, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/63903921

items.context:
Tara (white-fronted tern), Sterna striata, is native to New Zealand. A slender, pale-grey and white sea tern with a black cap separated from the black bill by a white forehead, and a deeply forked white tail.

In this photo: Black cap separated from the bill by a white forehead, pale grey back, black bill, long forked tail streamers.

Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A slender, pale-grey and white sea tern with a black cap separated from the black bill by a white forehead, and a deeply forked white tail.

media.alt: A slender pale-grey seabird with a black cap, white forehead and long forked tail stands on a rock
media.credit: Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:White-fronted_tern_(Sterna_striata)_(26822094987).jpg

items.context:
Tūī, Prosthemadera novaeseelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A blackbird-sized honeyeater that looks black at a distance but shines blue, green and bronze in good light. Two curled white tufts hang at the throat, with a lacy collar of fine white feathers on the neck.

In this photo: White throat tuft, metallic blue-green and bronze sheen on wings and back, lacy pale neck feathers.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A blackbird-sized honeyeater that looks black at a distance but shines blue, green and bronze in good light. Two curled white tufts hang at the throat, with a lacy collar of fine white feathers on the neck.

media.alt: A dark iridescent bird with a white tuft at its throat perches side-on on a weathered stump
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tui_(Prosthemadera_novaeseelandiae)_Tiritiri_Matangi_2.jpg

items.context:
Korimako (bellbird), Anthornis melanura, is found only in New Zealand. A slim, olive-green honeyeater with a short curved bill, a slightly forked tail and red eyes. It has no white tufts or wing bars.

In this photo: Duller olive-brown plumage without purple head gloss, narrow pale cheek stripe from bill base, red eye, curved bill.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A slim, olive-green honeyeater with a short curved bill, a slightly forked tail and red eyes. It has no white tufts or wing bars.

media.alt: A plain olive-brown songbird with a thin pale stripe below the eye perches on a pale dead branch
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Female_bellbird_perched_on_a_branch_(Ulva_Island).jpg

items.context:
Hihi (stitchbird), Notiomystis cincta, is found only in New Zealand. A small, fast-moving honeyeater that often cocks its tail like a wren, with a bold white wing bar and a thin, down-curved bill.

In this photo: Plain olive-brown plumage, white wing bar, cocked tail, no black head or yellow band.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small, fast-moving honeyeater that often cocks its tail like a wren, with a bold white wing bar and a thin, down-curved bill.

media.alt: A small olive-brown bird with a white bar on the wing and a raised tail perches on a twig
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Female_hihi_(stitchbird)_perched_on_a_twig.jpg

items.context:
Kererū (New Zealand pigeon), Hemiphaga novaeseelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A very large pigeon with iridescent green, bronze and purple upperparts sharply cut off from a clean white breast, and a red bill, eyes and feet.

In this photo: Iridescent green-purple upperparts, white belly, red bill; feeding on nīkau fruit.

Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A very large pigeon with iridescent green, bronze and purple upperparts sharply cut off from a clean white breast, and a red bill, eyes and feet.

Pīwakawaka (New Zealand fantail), Rhipidura fuliginosa, is found only in New Zealand. A small, restless bird that constantly fans its long tail. The common pied form has a grey head, white eyebrows, black and white bands on the throat and a cinnamon belly; the rare black form is almost all sooty black.

In this photo: White eyebrow and throat marks, buff underparts, long white-edged tail.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small, restless bird that constantly fans its long tail. The common pied form has a grey head, white eyebrows, black and white bands on the throat and a cinnamon belly; the rare black form is almost all sooty black.

media.alt: A small dark-headed bird with a buff belly perches on a twig with its long tail partly spread
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fantail_perched_on_a_twig,_looking_down_(Rotoroa_Island).jpg

Riroriro (grey warbler), Gerygone igata, is found only in New Zealand. A tiny, slim bird, olive-grey above and pale grey to off-white below, with a bright red eye and a fine black bill. The darker tail has white tips that show as a band in flight, and it often hovers at the edge of foliage.

In this photo: Very small, grey-olive above and pale below, thin bill, white tips to the tail.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A tiny, slim bird, olive-grey above and pale grey to off-white below, with a bright red eye and a fine black bill. The darker tail has white tips that show as a band in flight, and it often hovers at the edge of foliage.

media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Grey_warbler_clinging_to_a_twig.jpg

items.context:
Tauhou (silvereye), Zosterops lateralis, is native, having reached New Zealand on its own. A small olive-green songbird with an obvious ring of white feathers around the eye, a grey back and pinkish-buff flanks.

In this photo: White eye-ring, olive-green crown and wings, chestnut-buff flanks.

Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand (CC0).

practices.explanation: A small olive-green songbird with an obvious ring of white feathers around the eye, a grey back and pinkish-buff flanks.

media.alt: A small olive bird with a white eye-ring and warm brown flanks stands on a cut post

Miromiro (tomtit), Petroica macrocephala, is found only in New Zealand. A small, big-headed forest bird with short legs and a white wing bar that often perches on low branches. Males show a small white spot above the bill.

In this photo: Brown-grey head and back with no black, white wing bar, fawn-buff breast fading paler on the belly.

Photo: Darcy Whittaker (CC BY-NC 4.0).

practices.explanation: A small, big-headed forest bird with short legs and a white wing bar that often perches on low branches. Males show a small white spot above the bill.

media.credit: Photo: Darcy Whittaker, CC BY-NC 4.0, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/278939853

Toutouwai (North Island robin), Petroica longipes, is found only in New Zealand. A dark grey, upright, long-legged songbird with a pale patch on the lower breast and belly, often feeding on the ground and approaching people closely.

In this photo: Plump dark grey body, pale belly, long legs, large dark eye.

Photo: Tony Wills (CC BY 2.5).

practices.explanation: A dark grey, upright, long-legged songbird with a pale patch on the lower breast and belly, often feeding on the ground and approaching people closely.

media.alt: A fluffed-up dark grey bird with a pale belly perches among tangled twigs

Tītitipounamu (rifleman), Acanthisitta chloris, is found only in New Zealand. New Zealand's smallest bird: almost tailless, with a fine, slightly upturned bill and a pale eyebrow. It creeps up trunks and flicks its wings constantly.

In this photo: Tiny and stub-tailed; streaked brown-olive back and crown, white eyebrow, white underparts.

Photo: Melissa Boardman (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: New Zealand's smallest bird: almost tailless, with a fine, slightly upturned bill and a pale eyebrow. It creeps up trunks and flicks its wings constantly.

Pōpokotea (whitehead), Mohoua albicilla, is found only in New Zealand. A small, compact North Island songbird with a white head and underparts, brown-grey back, wings and tail, and a short dark bill. It usually travels in noisy flocks.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small, compact North Island songbird with a white head and underparts, brown-grey back, wings and tail, and a short dark bill. It usually travels in noisy flocks.

media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Whitehead_perched_on_a_branch.jpg

Mohua (yellowhead), Mohoua ochrocephala, is found only in New Zealand. A small South Island forest songbird with a bright canary-yellow head and breast, brown back, wings and tail, and a black bill and legs.

In this photo: Yellow head, grey-olive back and wings, yellowish tail edges, dark bill and legs.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A small South Island forest songbird with a bright canary-yellow head and breast, brown back, wings and tail, and a black bill and legs.

media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mohua_standing_on_a_branch_(Ulva_Island).jpg

Kōkako, Callaeas wilsoni, is found only in New Zealand. A large blue-grey songbird with a black face mask and small, bright blue wattles hanging from the base of the bill. It has long legs and a long tail and bounds through branches more than it flies.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A large blue-grey songbird with a black face mask and small, bright blue wattles hanging from the base of the bill. It has long legs and a long tail and bounds through branches more than it flies.

media.alt: A grey bird with blue wattles at the base of its bill faces the camera from a branch
media.credit: Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia, Public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kokako_standing_on_a_branch_(Tiritiri_Matangi).jpg

Tīeke (saddleback), Philesturnus rufusater (North Island) and Philesturnus carunculatus (South Island), is found only in New Zealand. Photo: Charles J. Sharp (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A glossy black songbird with a chestnut 'saddle' across the back and rump and fleshy orange-red wattles at the corners of the bill. North Island birds have a thin pale yellow line along the front edge of the saddle.

Ruru (morepork), Ninox novaeseelandiae, is native to New Zealand. A soft, low two-part 'more-pork' (or 'ru-ru') hoot at night, the second syllable dropping in pitch, repeated slowly and steadily.

practices.explanation: A soft, low two-part 'more-pork' (or 'ru-ru') hoot at night, the second syllable dropping in pitch, repeated slowly and steadily.

Kākā, Nestor meridionalis, is found only in New Zealand. A large olive-brown forest parrot with a grey-white crown, a heavy grey bill, crimson belly and under-tail, and red-orange under the wings.

Photo: Paul O'Shea (CC BY-SA 4.0).

practices.explanation: A large olive-brown forest parrot with a grey-white crown, a heavy grey bill, crimson belly and under-tail, and red-orange under the wings.

Kea, Nestor notabilis, is found only in New Zealand. A large olive-green mountain parrot with scalloped feathers, a long narrow grey-black upper bill and scarlet-orange under the wings.

Kākāpō, Strigops habroptilus, is found only in New Zealand. A very large, flightless, night-active parrot with moss-green plumage mottled with yellow and black, and a pale, owl-like whiskered face.

practices.explanation: A very large, flightless, night-active parrot with moss-green plumage mottled with yellow and black, and a pale, owl-like whiskered face.

Kākāriki (red-crowned parakeet), Cyanoramphus novaezelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. A bright emerald-green, long-tailed parakeet with a crimson forehead and crown, a crimson stripe through the eye, a red patch on each side of the rump and blue on the wing edge.

Photo: Pseudopanax at English Wikipedia (Public domain).

practices.explanation: A bright emerald-green, long-tailed parakeet with a crimson forehead and crown, a crimson stripe through the eye, a red patch on each side of the rump and blue on the wing edge.

practices.explanation: A sparrow-sized cuckoo with shining metallic green upperparts and white underparts crossed by dark green-bronze bars. No other New Zealand bird is iridescent green like this.

items.context:
Tūī, Prosthemadera novaeseelandiae, is found only in New Zealand. Melodious notes jumbled together with clicks, coughs and wheezes, some too high to hear well; the bell notes plus the 'junk' sounds in one phrase mean tūī rather than bellbird. Recordist identified this bird as male, but song is not a reliable sex cue.

Recording: Meena Haribal (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

media.alt: Busy, varied song: bursts of liquid bell-like notes mixed with loud clicks, cracks, wheezes and rasping noises, in short rapid phrases
media.credit: Recording: Meena Haribal, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, https://xeno-canto.org/957403

practices.explanation: Melodious notes jumbled together with clicks, coughs and wheezes, some too high to hear well; the bell notes plus the 'junk' sounds in one phrase mean tūī rather than bellbird. Recordist identified this bird as male, but song is not a reliable sex cue.

practices.explanation: Short, clear, bell-like phrases repeated in the same pattern each time (local dialect); clean ringing tone without the clicks and wheezes of tūī.

Miromiro (tomtit), Petroica macrocephala, is found only in New Zealand. A brief, high, cheerful 'ti-oly-oly-oly-ho' phrase at regular intervals. Full song is given by adult males; both sexes give short 'seet' calls.
